title: One-variable cutoff-kernel bound h(c) >= c^(-n) via the fundamental theorem of calculus
statement: Let n be a natural number, phi : R -> R, and eps, s, r, c real numbers. Assume eps > 0; phi is C^1 and nonincreasing, with phi(u) = 1 for u <= 1 and phi(u) = 0 for u >= 1 + eps; s > 0 and (1 + eps) s <= c <= r. Write phi' := deriv phi. Then 1/c^n <= integral_s^r (-(c/t * phi'(c/t)))/t/t^n dt, where the integral is the oriented interval integral from s to r.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (ε s r c : ℝ), 0 < ε → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → Antitone φ → (∀ u : ℝ, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → (∀ u : ℝ, 1 + ε ≤ u → φ u = 0) → 0 < s → (1 + ε) * s ≤ c → c ≤ r → 1 / c ^ n ≤ ∫ t in s..r, -(c / t * deriv φ (c / t)) / t / t ^ n
